## About our Flagship Accelerator

Back in 2010, 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) pioneered an accelerator program and shaped how venture capital fostered early-stage startups. Today, 500 Global continues to invest in founders, offering $150,000 in investment, founder-focused programming, growth and development curriculum, and tailored support. Our four-month in-person program is hosted in Silicon Valley, dedicated to scaling startups to new heights.

## What do founders get from the program?

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F3193e8e98d564353a0da6c6d58ee6665?width=80)

### Investment

Fuel your vision and lay the foundation for success with an investment that offers the crucial capital needed to build, launch, and quickly grow your startup. When your company is accepted to our Flagship Accelerator, we offer a seed investment of $150,000 for a 6% stake.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F7c6332a5ba574c3abe5c16f5fd702284?width=80)

### Community

Build and work with other founders navigating their startup journey, facing similar challenges, and growing together. The 500 founder community consists of 5,000+ founders hailing from diverse backgrounds, areas of expertise, and locations.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2Fa1155ea6da1743d8b499c23bf6e888b9?width=80)

### Mentorship & hands-on support

We bring together industry experts to help founders reach milestones faster and accelerate their problem-solving processes. Along with the 500 Global team of experienced operator-investors, alumni founder coaches, entrepreneurs in residence, mentors, and guest speakers provide expert guidance and real-world insights. Speakers include top domain experts on important topics such as distribution, design, data, fundraising, and more.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2Fae415a6376bb4a2f91cb8e46b1d41b58?width=80)

### Curriculum

Our curriculum emphasizes growth hacks and design best practices, guided by best-in-class operators. Key areas of focus include customer discovery, product-market fit, go-to-market strategies, pitch development, fundraising, and partnerships tailored for the modern founder and startup.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F44898dd838a74d97854e06d2ec4a145e?width=80)

### Network

Working with 500 Global means access to a vast network of investors, resources, mentorship, and market insights across multiple geographies. This support will be instrumental in navigating the complexities of entering new markets and leveraging opportunities on a global scale. With our global network at your fingertips, you’ll unlock unique growth opportunities.

## Exclusive perks & deals

As a 500 Global founder, you gain exclusive access to over $1M in credits in the 500 FounderHub, where free credits and exclusive discounts on AI tools, hosting, banking, cap table management and more await to elevate your startup.

But the benefits go beyond savings - FounderHub connects you with our firm, fellow founders, mentors, and the broader venture ecosystem, all dedicated to creating opportunities to drive your success.

## Program Details

This 12-week program was designed with you in mind, thoughtfully divided into three parts, meticulously designed to provide you with the best hands-on acceleration journey. Alongside this structured approach, you’ll also benefit from personalized **mentorship**, a vibrant **entrepreneurial community**, and the opportunity to apply newfound skills immediately to your startup, setting you on the path to **sustainable growth**.

Custom Button

Date

Location

The 500 Global Accelerator Program in Eurasia is tailor-made for ambitious tech startups operating in the dynamic **Eurasia region** and:

- Are in the early revenue stage
- Have a functional prototype
- Have the potential to address global markets
- Have a cross-functional team with market expertise
- Have a VC backing potential

## Here's what to expect

Tech startups that have direct or indirect operations in the following countries can apply:

Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia (the Czech Republic), Estonia, Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan (the Kyrgyz Republic), Latvia, Lithuania, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia,Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan.

#### Phase 1: In-Person (Apr 6 - 17, 2026)

### Foundations of Growth

Experience an immersive **2-week** journey in the dynamic city of **Tbilisi**, where you'll connect with fellow startup enthusiasts, seasoned mentors, and visionary partners.

During these transformative weeks, you'll actively participate in practical, hands-on sessions, receive invaluable one-on-one mentorship, and embark on a journey through a proven process of startup growth that includes:

- **Analytics:** Establishing analytics foundation and maximizing customer journey tracking.
- **Customer Development:** Integrating vital customer insights for impactful communication.
- **Metrics:** Setting clear objectives, and KPI reporting for confident data-based decisions.
- **Growth:** Tailoring B2C and B2B growth strategies.
- **Marketing:** Mastering sales funnel design and optimization.
- **Sales:** Creating a high-ROI sales team

The program Fee for **Phase 1 is $35,000 per startup**, excluding travel expenses. This fee covers the comprehensive support, mentorship, and resources provided throughout Phase 1.

By completing Phase 1, startups is expected to gain valuable insights, refine their strategies, and make informed decisions for successful market expansion.

#### Phase 2: Remote (Apr 20 - Jun 12, 2026)

### Growth Weeks

The following 8 weeks constitute the 'Big Growth' phase, during which you'll work closely with your dedicated mentor while launching tens of experiments for your business. This is where we tackle growth.

Here's what you'll learn:

- Advanced tailored B2B sales strategies, including account-based marketing and objection handling.
- Pipeline management, how to efficiently handle B2B sales pipelines, from lead generation to conversion.
- Negotiation & nurturing skills for lasting B2B client relationships.
- Conducting on-site and off-site analysis of your website, funnels, and marketing communication channels.
- Creating comprehensive testing protocols, validating tests, and gathering data.

Additionally, you'll participate in workshops with global experts covering:

- Mastering content, email, and SMS strategies for 'assets monetization'.
- Crafting and implementing retention strategies to maximize Customer Lifetime Value.
- Learnings on company finances 101: building a strong financial foundation and delving into financial projections, comprehensive reporting, and profit & loss mastery.

The program Fee for **Phase 1 is $35,000 per startup**, excluding travel expenses. This fee covers the comprehensive support, mentorship, and resources provided throughout Phase 1.

By completing Phase 1, startups is expected to gain valuable insights, refine their strategies, and make informed decisions for successful market expansion.

#### Phase 3: In-Person (Jun 15 - 26, 2026)

### Fundraising

Phase 3 represents the culmination of your journey as you come together in Tbilisi with your mentors and fellow startup founders.

These final two weeks are thoughtfully designed to prepare you for your fundraising efforts. You'll receive guidance on crafting a compelling pitch, designing an impactful deck, building an investor network, and formulating a comprehensive fundraising strategy.

This phase culminates in an exciting **Demo Day** **(June 25, 2026)** event, where you'll have the opportunity to present your company to a diverse audience of hundreds of local and international key ecosystem stakeholders. It's your chance to showcase your product in Tbilisi to propel your startup to new heights.

The program Fee for **Phase 1 is $35,000 per startup**, excluding travel expenses. This fee covers the comprehensive support, mentorship, and resources provided throughout Phase 1.

By completing Phase 1, startups is expected to gain valuable insights, refine their strategies, and make informed decisions for successful market expansion.

## The program offers founders

Through experiential learning and curated lessons from 500’s experts, participants will:

### Community

Starting a company is solitary and challenging. Working with other people going through the same challenges makes a huge difference. Founders who've gone through our program tell us that the 500 community is extremely valuable.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F3193e8e98d564353a0da6c6d58ee6665?width=80)

### Funding

Through the accelerator program you will have an opportunity for an investment of potentially **$100,000**.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2Fd603d292aef541c3b2f80ba655e3a916?width=80)

### Advice

You'll get access to a network of 1000+ founders, 200+ mentors, and our staff, who will give you guidance when you need it most. We've built startups before. We like to guide you to avoid making the same mistakes we did.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F23a9bdfea0b44af883318308af4f6298?width=80)

Our mentors will become a valuable extension of your growth team for 12 weeks. We'll work together as you prepare your business and product strategy, growth and metrics, and investor pitches.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F44898dd838a74d97854e06d2ec4a145e?width=80)

### Connections

Thanks to our extensive network, startups have the opportunity to build and grow their relationships and partnerships. Need an intro to a customer? Early access to a new platform feature? API access blocked? Stuck at the border? We have connections.

![](https://cdn.builder.io/api/v1/image/assets%2F26187a5473654c43ab7a1b7a54514e5c%2F10ea1650f2fa47fa8b951af69aa9fb65?width=80)

# Top Accelerator Programs for Tech Startups in 2025

Jan 4, 2025 9:51:23 AM[Luis Gonçalves](https://unicornbuilder.studio/blog/author/luis-gon%C3%A7alves)7 min read

As the tech startup ecosystem continues to evolve and expand, accelerator programs play an increasingly crucial role in nurturing and propelling promising ventures to success. In 2024, the landscape of accelerators has become more diverse and specialized, offering startups a wide range of options to boost their growth. This article explores the top 10 accelerator programs for tech startups in 2024, highlighting their unique features, benefits, and success stories.

## Accelerator Programs

1. Y Combinator (YC)

Y Combinator remains at the forefront of startup accelerators, continually adapting its program to meet the changing needs of the tech ecosystem.

Key Features:

- $500,000 investment for 7% equity
- 3-month intensive program
- Access to a vast network of alumni and investors
- Demo Day with high-profile investors

Notable Alumni: Airbnb, Dropbox, Stripe

YC's program focuses on rapid iteration and growth, emphasizing the importance of building something people want. In 2024, YC has expanded its remote participation options while maintaining its core philosophy of founder-to-founder advice and hands-on support.

2. Techstars

Techstars continues to be a global powerhouse in the accelerator space, with programs across multiple cities and industries.

Key Features:

- $20,000 investment for 6% equity, plus $100,000 convertible note
- 3-month program with mentorship-driven approach
- Access to Techstars' global network
- Industry-specific programs in various locations

Notable Alumni: SendGrid, DigitalOcean, ClassPass

In 2024, Techstars has further expanded its industry-specific programs, partnering with major corporations to offer targeted acceleration in areas like AI, blockchain, and sustainability tech.

3. 500 Startups

500 Startups has evolved into a venture capital firm with a strong accelerator component, known for its global approach and focus on diversity.

Key Features:

- $150,000 investment for 6% equity
- 4-month program
- Strong focus on growth marketing and international expansion
- Extensive global network across 75+ countries

Notable Alumni: Grab, Canva, Shippo

In 2024, 500 Startups has increased its focus on emerging markets and technologies, offering specialized tracks for fintech, healthtech, and climate tech startups.

4. Unicorn Boutique Accelerator

The Unicorn Boutique Accelerator has quickly risen to prominence, particularly for startups focusing on the Saudi and MENA markets.

Key Features:

- $500,000 to $1,000,000 investment for 5-15% equity
- 6-month intensive program
- Hands-on product development expertise
- Strong focus on the Scaleup Methodology

Notable Aspects: The Unicorn Boutique Accelerator stands out for its longer program duration and higher investment amounts. It's particularly well-suited for startups that have achieved product-market fit and are looking to scale rapidly.

In 2024, Unicorn Boutique has expanded its program to include specialized tracks for AI/ML, fintech, and sustainability-focused startups, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030 initiatives. The program's emphasis on the Scaleup Methodology provides startups with a comprehensive framework for growth, covering areas from digital sales strategies to organizational design.

5. Plug and Play

Plug and Play has established itself as a major player in the corporate innovation space, connecting startups with industry-leading corporations.

Key Features:

- No mandatory equity requirement
- 3-month industry-specific programs
- Strong corporate partnerships
- Global network with 35+ locations

Notable Alumni: Dropbox, PayPal, N26

In 2024, Plug and Play has further expanded its industry verticals, adding programs in emerging fields like quantum computing and advanced materials. Their no-equity model continues to attract startups looking for corporate partnerships and pilot opportunities.

6. Founders Factory

Founders Factory offers a unique model combining a startup accelerator with a corporate-backed incubator.

Key Features:

- £30,000 investment plus £220,000 in-kind services for 7% equity
- 6-month program
- Hands-on operational support from a team of experts
- Strong corporate partnerships for pilot opportunities

Notable Alumni: Hark, Vyking, Zebra Fuel

In 2024, Founders Factory has expanded its sector-specific programs, partnering with additional corporations to offer targeted acceleration in areas like clean energy, edutech, and advanced healthcare.

7. AngelPad

AngelPad maintains its reputation as a "anti-demo day" accelerator, focusing on intensive mentorship and long-term company building.

Key Features:

- $120,000 investment for 7% equity
- 3-month program with a focus on fundamentals
- Small, selective cohorts (typically 15 companies)
- Emphasis on building sustainable businesses rather than quick exits

Notable Alumni: Postmates, Vungle, Pipedrive

In 2024, AngelPad has further refined its approach, offering even more personalized mentorship and introducing a post-program support phase to help startups navigate their next stages of growth.

8. Alchemist Accelerator

Alchemist continues to focus exclusively on enterprise startups, offering a specialized program for B2B ventures.

Key Features:

- $36,000 investment for 5% equity
- 6-month program
- Strong focus on enterprise sales and go-to-market strategies
- Extensive network of enterprise customers and investors

Notable Alumni: LaunchDarkly, Rigetti Computing, Privacera

In 2024, Alchemist has expanded its program to include more international startups, recognizing the global nature of enterprise technology. They've also introduced specialized tracks for cybersecurity and AI for business applications.

SOSV operates multiple accelerator programs across different verticals, including HAX (hardware), IndieBio (biotech), and Chinaccelerator (cross-border).

Key Features:

- Investment amounts vary by program ($100,000 - $250,000)
- Program lengths vary (3-6 months)
- Specialized resources for hardware, biotech, and cross-border expansion
- Global network across multiple tech hubs

Notable Alumni: GetAround, BitMEX, Perfect Day

In 2024, SOSV has further expanded its thematic accelerators, launching new programs focused on climate tech and deep tech. Their multi-program approach continues to attract diverse startups across various technology sectors.

As space technology becomes increasingly important, the Techstars Space Accelerator has emerged as a leading program in this niche.

Key Features:

- 3-month program focused on space-related technologies
- Partnerships with NASA, U.S. Air Force, and leading aerospace companies
- Access to specialized mentors and resources in the space industry

Notable Alumni: Morpheus Space, Pixxel, Infinite Composites

In 2024, the Techstars Space Accelerator has expanded its focus to include technologies with dual-use applications in space and terrestrial markets, recognizing the growing convergence of space tech with other industries.

## Choosing the Right Accelerator for Your Startup

When considering which accelerator program is right for your tech startup, several factors should be taken into account:

1. Stage of Your Startup: Some accelerators, like Y Combinator and Unicorn Boutique, are well-suited for startups that have already achieved some traction, while others like Founders Factory are great for very early-stage ventures.
2. Industry Focus: Programs like Alchemist (enterprise) or Techstars Space have specific industry focuses that can provide targeted resources and connections.
3. Geographical Considerations: While many programs have gone remote, some still offer significant benefits for being on-site. Consider whether you're looking to expand into specific markets (e.g., Unicorn Boutique for MENA).

5. Network and Partnerships: Consider the strength and relevance of the accelerator's network to your startup's needs.
6. Program Length and Intensity: Some programs are short and intense (3 months), while others like Unicorn Boutique offer longer engagements (6 months).
7. Post-Program Support: Look into what kind of support is offered after the formal program ends.
8. Alumni Success Stories: Research the track record of the accelerator and the success of its alumni in your industry.

6. Global Expansion: Many accelerators are expanding their geographical reach, either through remote programs or new physical locations.

metadata.description: 500 Global is an early-stage venture fund and seed accelerator founded in 2010 by Dave McClure and Christine Tsai. The fund admitted a first "class" of twelve startups to its incubator office in Mountain View, California in February 2011. They expanded to a second class of 21 in June 2011 and a third class of 34 in October 2011. 500 Global has $2.3 billion in assets under management (AUM) as of March 2024. Notable companies 500 Global invested in include Eat App, IDreamBooks, Little Eye Labs, myGengo, Cypheme, Cucumbertown, Visual.ly, Canva, Convoz, Udemy, RidePal and Aircall. In 2012, 500 Global acquired Mexican.VC, an accelerator in Mexico City, expects to substantially ramp up its investment in Mexico. Through its investment in Alta Ventures, 500 Global planned to have better access to deal flow in this region. 500 Global LATAM is directed by Santiago Zavala and has startups like Platzi in its portfolio. As of February 2021, 500 Global had invested in over 2,400 companies including Eat App, IDreamBooks, Little Eye Labs, myGengo, Cypheme, Cucumbertown, Visual.ly, Canva, Convoz, Udemy, RidePal and Aircall. As of August 2015, more than 20% of the companies had participated in other incubators, 20–30% were based outside the United States, and over 60 had been acquired. As of 2015, some of the firm's active companies were Credit Karma, Twilio, GrabTaxi, and Talkdesk. The exits include $403M acquisition of MakerBot by Stratasys, $350M acquisition of Wildfire by Google, $200M acquisition of Viki by Rakuten, and $117M acquisition of Simple by BBVA. 500 Global has investment partners and advisors from all over the world, e.g. Jassim Alseddiqi, Enis Hulli (Turkey), Binh Tran (Vietnam), and Tilo Bonow (Germany). A famous partner, Monique Woodard from Black Founders, left the early-stage venture fund in 2018. 500 Global has locations in San Francisco, Mexico City, Miami, Dubai, Bahrain, Istanbul, Seoul, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Bangkok and Ho Chi Minh City. In 2015, they announced they would be starting a three-month growth program in London, UK as well as a pre-accelerator in Oslo, Norway. Full global programs have expanded to Japan, Taiwan, Singapore, Cambodia, Georgia, Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Canada. In July 2017, co-founder Dave McClure resigned as general partner of all funds and entities managed by 500 Startups amid allegations of sexual harassment. In March 2018, 500 Startups announced that it chose Downtown Miami as its first East Coast U.S. outpost. In July 2019, Courtney Powell was named Chief Operating Officer of the firm. In November 2020, 500 Startups formed a two-year partnership with Khmer Enterprise, a unit under the Cambodian Ministry of Economy and Finance. Through the Angkor 500 initiative, the firms will bring together founders throughout Cambodia to form teams and technology companies. In September 2021, 500 Startups announced their rebranding to 500 Global and the closing of a $140M global flagship fund – the firm’s largest fund to date–bringing assets under management to $1.8B. The firm has stated it is expanding its investment strategy beyond the accelerator and seed stage. In October 2021, 500 Global had its first fully virtual accelerator class. In early 2023, the firm announced that it has launched an accelerator program in Tbilisi, Georgia as a part of its expansion in Eastern Europe.

Taking the steps for your own startup can be as exciting as it is challenging..In this article, we will talk about the best startup accelerators and programs that support startups and enable them to access the mentorship they need in the early stages. Our list also includes several leading corporate startup programs, such as [Siemens for Startups](https://lp.startupblink.com/siemens-solid-edge/?utm_campaign=blog&utm_medium=blog&utm_source=blog), and many others, as alternatives to traditional startup accelerators.

## What are Startup Accelerators?

![best startup accelerators & programs](https://www.startupblink.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Ghers-@-Go-Fest-3-1024x682.jpg)

Let’s start with the definition of accelerator programs:

Startup accelerators are fixed-term, cohort-based programs that help early-stage companies and entrepreneurs accelerate the growth of their businesses. These programs offer a range of support services and resources, typically in exchange for equity or a small investment in the company.

Being connected to the ecosystem, learning from the mistakes of others, networking with experienced stakeholders, knowing how to secure funding and what options are available for it is as valuable as gold when establishing your own startup. Accelerator programs can provide you with these resources and therefore are one of the most crucial parts that hold the ecosystem together. They enable you to quickly get acquainted with the ecosystem and adapt to it.

## Public Sector Startup Programs & Accelerators

In this section we spotlight a selection of public‑sector startup programs and accelerators. These are initiatives that are led, funded, or co‑managed by government entities. The examples illustrate how policy makers across the world are actively seeding innovation, de‑risking early‑stage ventures, and connecting founders to critical resources such as capital, mentorship, and international markets.

### Wadi Accelerator

**Focus: Oman**

**Equity Taken: Varies depending on investment**

The **Wadi Accelerator** is an initiative under the **Oman Technology Fund (OTF)**, aimed at supporting startups in the acceleration stage. Based in Oman, Wadi offers a structured program that includes funding, expert mentorship, and access to a regional and international network of investors and partners. The accelerator is designed to help startups with a validated product scale quickly by providing tailored support in areas such as business development, product refinement, and market access. [You can apply here.](https://www.otf.om/)

### iNNpulsa Colombia Accelerator

**Focus: Colombia**

## How to Prepare to Apply for Accelerators & Startup Programs

The process often begins with an online application form. This form usually requests basic information about the startup, such as the team members, business idea, target market, revenue model, and any existing traction or milestones.

Many accelerators require applicants to submit a pitch deck, which is an overview of the startup, including its problem statement, solution, market size, competitive analysis , revenue model, and other key details.

Another potential step while applying for a startup program or accelerator can be a video pitch. This is an opportunity for founders to present their business in a more dynamic format, allowing the accelerator team to get a better sense of the team’s passion and the startup’s value proposition.

Shortlisted applicants may be invited for interviews. The purpose is to dive deeper into the details of the startup, assess the team’s capabilities, and evaluate how well the startup aligns with the goals of the accelerator program.

If you will go through an interview process, we recommend reading comments and advice from founders who have previously participated in the interview. You can find numerous resources on the internet about this; here’s an example: [YC Interview Guide.](https://www.ycombinator.com/interviews)
